source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building fire-safety checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Include the date and time the inspection was conducted.
3. Record the exact location of the building, including address and unit number if applicable.
4. Identify the specific fire-safety systems and equipment that were inspected (e.g., fire alarms, sprinklers, emergency exits, fire extinguishers, smoke detectors).
5. List each failed safety check separately.
6. For each failure, specify the nature of the problem (e.g., sprinkler head blocked, alarm siren not audible, extinguisher pressure gauge below safe level).
7. Note any observed indications of non-compliance with relevant fire safety codes and standards.
8. Include photographs or diagrams, if possible, to support your findings.
9. Detail any immediate actions taken to resolve the issues or mitigate risk, e.g., temporary measures, notifications to the responsible parties.
10. Include a statement of whether or not the building remains safe for occupancy.
11. If the building is unsafe, note
